fullPassage: The expression "Moveable Feast" originally referred to the changing date of religious celebrations. It was later adopted by Ernest Hemingway to describe his experience of living in Paris. We use the term Moveable Feast to conceptualize the potentiality to connect with people, ideas, and information at any time and in any place. In the Digital Age, information circulates and travels not only in a straight line from official media outlets to consumers but has the potential to move from anyone to everyone else. The Moveable Feast is a table filled with information "dishes" that have been prepared by participating members of the feast. Each person may try a slice of everyone else's dish. Furthermore, this feast moves around the entire world and interacts with billions of other feasts-of-digits, complete with servings of information that are monitored by platforms and governments. At any given point in time, each person has the potential to connect with any other person by sampling their information, and perhaps by "dishing dirt" of their own, or by rejecting dishes that are not particularly tasty. This feast features all the components of social interaction in complex, dynamic information environments; as Hemingway most aptly described, "it stays with you" wherever you go.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ② conceptualizing → to conceptualize: 'use the term ~ to +동사원형'은 '~을 하기 위해 그 용어를 쓴다'는 목적을 나타내는 to부정사예요. 그래서 동사원형 앞에 to가 필요해요.
det.analysis:
✅ ② conceptualizing — 원문은 to conceptualize. 'We use the term Moveable Feast to conceptualize ...'는 '개념화하기 위해 그 용어를 쓴다'는 목적의 to부정사예요. 목적을 나타낼 때는 「to + 동사원형」을 써야 하므로 conceptualizing(동명사)은 틀려요 ←정답

❌ ① referred — 'originally referred to'는 과거시제(가리켰다)로 정상이에요.

❌ ③ circulates — 주어 information은 셀 수 없는 명사라 단수 취급, 단수동사 circulates가 맞아요.

❌ ④ filled — 'a table filled with ~'는 '~로 가득 찬 식탁'으로, 식탁이 채워지는 대상이라 과거분사 filled가 맞아요.
det.tip: 목적의 to부정사: to conceptualize (conceptualizing ✕)

det.korean: ④ what → that: 앞에 dishes(요리들)라는 꾸밈받는 명사(선행사)가 있으므로 관계대명사 that/which를 써야 해요. what은 선행사를 포함하는 관계사라 앞에 명사가 오면 쓸 수 없어요.

✅ ④ what are not particularly tasty — 원문은 that are not particularly tasty. 바로 앞 dishes(요리들)를 꾸며 주는 관계절이에요. 이렇게 앞에 꾸밈받는 명사(선행사)가 있으면 that(또는 which)을 써요. what은 '~하는 것'처럼 선행사를 이미 품고 있어서 앞에 dishes가 있으면 쓸 수 없어요 ←정답

❌ ① circulates — information(셀 수 없는 명사) + 단수동사 circulates, 정상이에요.

❌ ② prepared — 'have been prepared'의 과거분사 부분이라 정상이에요.

det.korean: ② producers → consumers: 공식 매체에서 정보가 직선으로 흘러가 '받는' 쪽은 소비자(consumers)예요. '생산자(producers)'는 정보를 만드는 쪽이라 흐름의 도착점으로는 어색해요.

❌ ① connect — '사람·생각·정보와 연결되다'로 문맥에 맞아요.

❌ ③ prepared — '참여 구성원들이 준비한 요리'로 자연스러워요.

questions.passage: The expression "Moveable Feast" __________. It was later adopted by Ernest Hemingway to describe his experience of living in Paris. We use the term Moveable Feast to conceptualize the potentiality to connect with people, ideas, and information at any time and in any place. In the Digital Age, information circulates and travels not only in a straight line from official media outlets to consumers but has the potential to move from anyone to everyone else. The Moveable Feast is a table filled with information "dishes" that have been prepared by participating members of the feast. Each person may try a slice of everyone else's dish. Furthermore, this feast moves around the entire world and interacts with billions of other feasts-of-digits, complete with servings of information that are monitored by platforms and governments. At any given point in time, each person has the potential to connect with any other person by sampling their information, and perhaps by "dishing dirt" of their own, or by rejecting dishes that are not particularly tasty. This feast features all the components of social interaction in complex, dynamic information environments; as Hemingway most aptly described, "it stays with you" wherever you go.
questions.stem:
다음 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 [조건]에 맞게 영어로 쓰시오. (주어 The expression을 제외한 술어 부분만 쓸 것)

"그 표현은 원래 종교 기념일의 변하는 날짜를 가리켰다."

[조건] (1) celebrations, changing, date, of, originally, referred, religious, the, to 를 모두 사용
       (2) 정확히 9단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: '~을 가리켰다'는 refer to의 과거형 referred to예요. '원래'는 부사 originally를 동사 앞에 놓아요.
det.analysis:
핵심은 '가리키다 = refer to'이고, 과거라서 referred to예요.

단계별로: '원래'를 뜻하는 부사 originally를 맨 앞에 → referred to(가리켰다) → 무엇을? the changing date(변하는 날짜) → of religious celebrations(종교 기념일의).

그래서 'originally referred to the changing date of religious celebrations'(9단어)가 돼요. refer 다음에 전치사 to가 꼭 필요하다는 점을 기억하세요.
det.tip: refer to의 과거형 referred to = ~을 가리켰다
